solution:
The roots must satisfy \(\{\alpha^2,\beta^2\}=\{\alpha,\beta\}\).
Case 1: \(\alpha^2=\alpha,\ \beta^2=\beta\), so each root is 0 or 1. The pairs \((0,0),(0,1),(1,1)\) give \(x^2,\ x^2-x,\ x^2-2x+1\), which is 3 equations.
Case 2: \(\alpha^2=\beta,\ \beta^2=\alpha\) with \(\alpha\neq\beta\). Then \(\alpha^4=\alpha\Rightarrow\alpha^3=1\), so the roots are \(\omega,\omega^2\), giving \(x^2+x+1\), which is 1 equation.
Total \(3+1=4\), option B.
note: Key 4 is right (x^2, x^2-x, (x-1)^2, x^2+x+1), but the solution says -1 gives roots; alpha=-1 forces beta=1 and beta^2=1 is not -1, so -1 is not a valid case.

solution:
\(D=(a+b+c)^2-4(a+b)\cdot\dfrac{c}{2}=(a+b+c)^2-2c(a+b)\).
Expanding, \(D=(a+b)^2+2c(a+b)+c^2-2c(a+b)=(a+b)^2+c^2\).
Since \(c\neq0\), \(D>0\), so the roots are real and unequal, option B.
note: discriminant = (a+b)^2+c^2 >0 for c!=0. Stored (a+b-c)^2+2c^2 is false (a=b=c=1: 3 vs 5).

solution:
Let \(f(x)=x^2-3x+1\). Its discriminant is \(9-4=5>0\), so \(f\) has real roots.
At a root \(f(x)=0\), so \(|f(x)|=0\).
Since \(|f(x)|\geq0\) always, the minimum value is 0, option B.
note: x^2-3x+1 has real roots (disc 5>0) so |.| reaches 0. Stored solution minimises the unabsoluted quadratic and gets 5/4 (really -5/4 at the vertex), contradicting option B.

solution:
Equal roots in \(x^2+bx+a=0\) give \(b^2=4a\), and the repeated root is \(x=-\dfrac{b}{2}\).
This root must satisfy \(ax^2+x+b=0\): \(\dfrac{ab^2}{4}-\dfrac{b}{2}+b=0\Rightarrow b\left(\dfrac{ab}{4}+\dfrac12\right)=0\).
If \(b\neq0\): \(ab=-2\). With \(a=\dfrac{b^2}{4}\) this gives \(b^3=-8\), so \(b=-2,\ a=1\).
Then \(2a^2+b=2-2=0\). (If \(b=0\) then \(a=0\) and again \(2a^2+b=0\).) Option A.
note: Key 0 right (a=1, b=-2). Stored solution takes b=+2sqrt(a), root -b/2, then a^(3/2)=-1 and a=1, which is false; the working branch is b=-2sqrt(a).

solution:
The roots \(\alpha,\beta\) must be unchanged on squaring, so \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=\alpha+\beta\) ... (i) and \(\alpha^2\beta^2=\alpha\beta\).
The second gives \(\alpha\beta(\alpha\beta-1)=0\), so \(\alpha=0\) or \(\beta=0\) or \(\alpha\beta=1\).
If \(\alpha=0\) (or \(\beta=0\)), (i) gives the other root as 0 or 1: roots \((0,0)\) and \((0,1)\).
If \(\alpha\beta=1\), (i) becomes \(s^2-2=s\) with \(s=\alpha+\beta\), so \(s=2\) or \(-1\): roots \((1,1)\) or \((\omega,\omega^2)\).
In total 4 quadratic equations, option B.
note: Key 4 right. Stored step turns alpha^2beta^2=alpha*beta into 2beta(alpha*beta-1)=0; correct is alpha*beta(alpha*beta-1)=0.

solution:
\(\alpha+\beta=-\dfrac34,\ \alpha\beta=\dfrac74\).
\(\alpha^{-2}+\beta^{-2}=\dfrac{(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta}{(\alpha\beta)^2}\).
Numerator \(=\dfrac{9}{16}-\dfrac{7}{2}=-\dfrac{47}{16}\); denominator \(=\dfrac{49}{16}\).
So the value is \(-\dfrac{47}{49}\), option C.

The equation is \((ab-ca)x^2+(bc-ab)x+(ca-bc)=0\).
The coefficients sum to 0, so \(x=1\) is a root. Equal roots means both roots are 1, so the product is 1: \(ca-bc=ab-ca\).
Then \(2ca=ab+bc\); dividing by \(abc\) gives \(\dfrac2b=\dfrac1c+\dfrac1a\).
So \(a,b,c\) are in HP, option C.
note: x=1 is a root (coefficients sum to 0) so equal roots means product 1, giving 2ca=ab+bc, i.e. 2/b=1/a+1/c. Stored 1/a+1/c=1/(2b) is wrong and it cites an outside Q31.

solution:
Since \(|x^2|=|x|^2\), put \(u=|x|\ge0\): \(u^2+u-6=0\Rightarrow(u+3)(u-2)=0\), so \(u=2\).
Hence \(x=2\) or \(x=-2\), and both satisfy the equation.
The roots are real with sum \(2+(-2)=0\), option C.
note: Key C right (roots +-2, sum 0). Stored solution lists roots -3,2 and 3,-2 (3 and -3 fail their cases) and has a stray =20.

solution:
\(\alpha+\beta=-3,\ \alpha\beta=\dfrac k2\), so \(\dfrac\alpha\beta+\dfrac\beta\alpha=\dfrac{9-k}{k/2}=\dfrac{18}{k}-2\).
For \(k<0\), \(\dfrac{18}{k}<0\) and tends to \(0\) as \(k\to-\infty\), so the expression stays below \(-2\) and approaches \(-2\).
The least upper bound is \(-2\) (not attained), and it is the only option that bounds the expression above, option B.
note: Key -2 is the only sensible option but the expression 18/k-2 is below -2 for every k<0, so -2 is an unattained upper bound, not a maximum; the stored text calls it the greatest value.
